canonical_statement: EHR2Dial-Triage was introduced as an EHR-to-dialogue framework and benchmark for multi-turn emergency-department triage with explicit role-based and temporal information boundaries.
The benchmark evaluates information elicitation separately from downstream use of a completed dialogue for five-level ESI prediction and patient-facing closing generation.
The frozen benchmark corpus contains 4,041 encounters from 3,888 unique patients, and every encounter has a recorded five-level ESI label.
Recorded ESI composition in the frozen cohort was 16.73% ESI-1, 30.83% ESI-2, 42.27% ESI-3, 9.85% ESI-4, and 0.32% ESI-5.
Encounter information available no later than the generation cutoff is partitioned into clinician-visible information C_i and patient-reportable information P_i.
Clinician-visible information includes selected demographics, recorded triage fields, initial measurements, and eligible prior-record information available at dialogue onset.
Patient-reportable information includes elicitable symptom history, associated symptoms, home medications, allergies, and relevant medical history that is not directly exposed to the clinician model.
Post-triage events and the recorded ESI label are excluded from both clinician-visible and patient-reportable information and cannot condition dialogue generation.
The patient persona controls non-clinical communication characteristics such as verbosity, phrasing style, recall confidence, and response detail without changing the patient clinical fact set.

Dialogue generation alternates a clinician model conditioned on clinician-visible information and public dialogue history with a patient model conditioned on patient-reportable information, persona, and the current dialogue.
A verifier maps accepted clinical disclosures to normalized atomic facts and links each accepted fact to an eligible source in C_i or P_i.
Each accepted disclosure retains its normalized fact identifier, supporting EHR source, round index, and speaker role, yielding machine-readable event-turn lineage.
Only facts originating from patient-reportable information P_i receive information-acquisition credit in the benchmark metrics.
Future-hidden fields are withheld from dialogue roles and used to detect post-triage leakage, while evaluation-only fields are withheld from roles and used only for labels or case characterization.
Benchmark validation checks role-consistent source realization, progressive disclosure of patient-reportable information, and predictive relevance of acquired information.
EHR2Dial-Triage uses a bounded, variable-length interaction budget to limit interview length and make clinician-model comparisons more comparable.

In Experiment I, each clinician model uses the same patient simulator, fact bank, disclosure policy, verifier, stopping rule, and ten-round budget; eligible patient facts, recorded ESI, and post-triage events remain hidden from the clinician model.
FACT COV@t is computed as within-encounter cumulative coverage of eligible patient-reportable facts and then macro-averaged across encounters, giving each encounter equal weight.

HISTORY MED COV@t measures cumulative coverage of eligible medical-history and home-medication facts; encounters with no eligible fact in this subset are excluded because their recall denominator is zero.

A fixed patient-disjoint multinomial logistic-regression reader is trained once and held unchanged across clinician models and checkpoints to measure how the ESI distribution changes as facts accumulate.

In Experiment II, every model receives the same completed speaker-labeled dialogue without the recorded ESI label, reference closing, separately serialized EHR fields, source identifiers, provenance annotations, verifier decisions, or post-triage information, and returns a five-class score vector, discrete ESI prediction, and concise closing.
Under-triage is defined as a predicted ESI value greater than the recorded ESI value because larger ESI numbers denote lower assigned urgency.
Patient-facing closing generation is evaluated with dialogue-grounded Key Recall and Grounded Precision, reference-similarity metrics BERTScore F1, ROUGE-L, and BLEU-4, and corpus-level Distinct-2.
Unless otherwise stated, Appendix C metrics are computed at the encounter level and macro-averaged over 1,013 evaluation encounters.
Catastrophic under-triage is defined as predicting ESI 4 or 5 for an encounter recorded as ESI 1 or 2.
Model-reported confidence is defined as the maximum value in the parsed five-class ESI score vector.

In the authors’ comparison of representative resources, EHR2Dial-Triage is marked as supporting a reusable generator, patient-level EHR grounding, event-turn lineage, and temporal tracing, while the other listed resources do not combine all four.

canonical_statement: MedGemma-1.5-4B never assigns ESI 4 or 5 in the evaluated predictions, so the paper reports no severe-under-triage confidence value for that model.
GPT-5.6 and Claude Fable 5 show lower rates of multi-level under-triage than several open-weight models in the paper’s severity analysis.
The corpus-validation analyses evaluate internal benchmark design and do not establish clinical validity or readiness for deployment.

The frozen cohort is a deliberately selected, acuity-enriched subset of MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2, so its label mix and benchmark performance should not be interpreted as real-world ESI prevalence or deployment performance.

Information acquisition, ESI prediction, evidence grounding, and patient-facing communication behave as distinct dimensions of model performance, and strong performance on one does not necessarily imply strong performance on the others.

The authors argue that safe clinical dialogue requires more than a final prediction: the system must identify missing information, elicit relevant evidence, recognize changes in urgency, and communicate the immediate plan clearly.
The authors recommend that safety evaluation consider under-triage severity, confidence reliability, and escalation or human-review mechanisms when uncertainty or risk is high.
Future work proposed by the authors includes clinician-adjudicated safety evaluation, multi-institutional validation, and richer assessment of patient-facing communication.
The paper states that code is available at https://github.com/illidanlab/elicited.
